title: Malformed-daily-bar hygiene: non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #70 (api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. PR #70 fixed the malformed-latest-daily-bar hazard (NaN open/high/low/close silently corrupting signal computation, e.g. `evaluate_trigger`'s `today_close > prior_high` quietly evaluating False instead of raising) for `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` via `app.signals.engine.drop_malformed_daily_bars`, applied both in `app/api/routers/stocks.py` and inside `analyse()` itself. The review found the same class of hazard is not fully addressed at every other place a malformed bar could reach signal-adjacent computation.

checklist.step: GET /api/portfolio/risk's exit-flag pipeline (app/api/routers/portfolio.py::get_risk -> app/portfolio/exits.py::evaluate_exit_flags, which internally calls protective_stop/autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse and does its own `latest_close < stop` comparison) reads `e.daily_ohlcv` from app/portfolio/pricing.py without ever passing it through drop_malformed_daily_bars (or an equivalent). app/portfolio/pricing.py::_latest_close already excludes a position outright when the very latest bar's `close` is NaN (the one specific failure mode observed so far), so that exact case can't reach evaluate_exit_flags today -- but a malformed bar earlier in the history, or one with NaN open/high/low but a real close, would still flow through unfiltered, risking the same NaN-silently-evaluates-False hazard this PR just fixed for /analysis (e.g. a silently suppressed 'stop_hit' flag via `latest_close < stop` on a NaN-poisoned EMA/autoenvelope computation). Extend the same filtering to this path for consistency.

Neither this PR's fix nor any pre-existing code filters `weekly_ohlcv` for malformed bars anywhere (evaluate_tide, used by both /analysis and /risk's tide_flipped_bearish flag, reads weekly_ohlcv['close'] directly with no NaN guard). The observed malformed-bar condition has so far only been reported on daily data from yfinance, so this is speculative -- track it and revisit if a malformed weekly bar is ever actually observed, mirroring the already-documented decision to leave GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history's raw daily bars unfiltered absent an observed bug there.

decisions.decision: Extended `app.signals.engine.drop_malformed_daily_bars` filtering to GET /api/portfolio/risk's pipeline by importing and calling the existing function directly in `app/api/routers/portfolio.py::get_risk`, rather than moving it to a new shared module or duplicating it in `app.portfolio`.
decisions.rationale: `app.portfolio.exits` already imports from `app.signals` (`triple_screen.evaluate_tide`/`validate_weekly_ohlcv_columns`, `impulse.evaluate_impulse`) for the exact same kind of shared domain logic, so `portfolio` -> `signals` is an established, non-circular dependency direction in this codebase -- there's no existing prohibition on it that a move would be working around. `drop_malformed_daily_bars` is also already public (not underscore-prefixed) and already imported directly from `app.signals.engine` by `app/api/routers/stocks.py`, so calling it the same way from `app/api/routers/portfolio.py` matches an existing, working precedent at the same architectural layer (API router) rather than introducing a new one. A move to a standalone module (e.g. `app.data` or a new `app.signals.ohlcv_hygiene`) was considered and rejected: it would touch more call sites/imports for no behavioral benefit, and the function's docstring and rationale are already tightly coupled to the specific `analyse()`/Screen 2-3 hazard it was written for, which is still accurate context even when reused from the risk pipeline. Filtering is applied at the router level (mirroring `app/api/routers/stocks.py::get_analysis`'s identical pattern) rather than inside `app.portfolio.exits.evaluate_exit_flags` itself, since `protective_stop` is also called directly from the router (before `evaluate_exit_flags`) and needs the same filtered frame.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Filtering inside `evaluate_exit_flags`/`protective_stop` themselves (rejected: `protective_stop` is called twice per position in `get_risk` -- once directly, once inside `evaluate_exit_flags` -- so filtering at the router once and reusing the filtered frame avoids a redundant `dropna` pass and keeps both call sites demonstrably fed the same corrected history, the same reasoning already used for the EMA(13)-sharing between them).

decisions.decision: Hardened `drop_malformed_daily_bars` itself to only `dropna(subset=...)` over whichever of open/high/low/close columns are actually present in the input frame, instead of unconditionally naming all four.
decisions.rationale: Extending the filter into `get_risk` surfaced a latent bug: `pandas.DataFrame.dropna(subset=[...])` raises a bare `KeyError` (not the documented `ValueError`) when a named subset column doesn't exist in the frame at all -- a distinct failure mode from the NaN-*value* one this function targets. Two of `tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py`'s existing fixtures intentionally construct a daily frame missing the `low` column outright to exercise `app.portfolio.risk.validate_daily_ohlcv_columns`'s documented `ValueError` -> exclude-the-position path; calling `drop_malformed_daily_bars` before that validation (as this task's router change now does) broke both, replacing the intended graceful 200-with-empty-positions response with an unhandled 500. Restricting the `dropna` subset to columns that actually exist preserves this function's own NaN-row-dropping behavior unchanged for every existing caller (whose frames always have all four columns) while leaving a genuinely missing column for the caller's own column-presence check to raise its documented error for, matching the same division of responsibility `validate_daily_ohlcv_columns`/`validate_weekly_ohlcv_columns` already establish elsewhere in this codebase (validate columns before touching them; let a NaN *value* rather than a missing column be this function's own concern).
decisions.alternatives_considered: Reordering the router so column validation ran before `drop_malformed_daily_bars` was considered and rejected: `drop_malformed_daily_bars` needs to run on the *full* frame before `protective_stop`'s own internal `.iloc[:-1]` slicing and length check for correctness (see the other decision entry on this task), so a pre-check would have to duplicate `validate_daily_ohlcv_columns`'s exact column set at the router layer instead of fixing the one place (`drop_malformed_daily_bars`) that was actually fragile.

decisions.decision: Deferred applying `drop_malformed_daily_bars` (or an equivalent) to `weekly_ohlcv` rather than proactively filtering it now.
decisions.rationale: The malformed-bar condition this whole task's filtering defends against is a specific, *observed* yfinance behavior (an unsettled latest daily bar coming back with NaN OHLC) discovered via a real frontend crash on `api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators` -- it has never been observed on weekly data. The checklist item itself frames this as speculative and explicitly points at the existing precedent of leaving GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history's raw daily bars unfiltered absent an observed bug there (docs/tasks/api-stocks-history-followups.json) as the model to mirror. Proactively filtering `weekly_ohlcv` everywhere `evaluate_tide` is called (`app.signals.engine.analyse`, `app.portfolio.exits.evaluate_exit_flags`'s two calls) would also be materially more invasive than the daily-side fix: `evaluate_tide`'s current-vs-previous-tide comparison in `evaluate_exit_flags` relies on precomputed MACD/EMA series staying index-aligned with `weekly_ohlcv` across a `.iloc[:-1]` slice (see that function's own docstring), so dropping rows from `weekly_ohlcv` without also re-deriving those series consistently risks introducing a subtler alignment bug in defense of a condition that has never actually occurred. Tracking it here (this checklist item, left in the task board rather than closed as literally 'not applicable') means it will actually get picked up if a malformed weekly bar is ever observed in practice, per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Proactively filtering `weekly_ohlcv` the same way as `daily_ohlcv` (rejected per the rationale above: speculative fix for an unobserved condition, non-trivial to do correctly given the precomputed-series-sharing between `evaluate_tide` calls in `evaluate_exit_flags`, and against this codebase's own established precedent of fixing observed problems rather than every theoretically-possible one).

comments.summary: Blocking regression: get_risk's new `daily_ohlcv = drop_malformed_daily_bars(e.daily_ohlcv)` can drop the position's *latest* (today's) bar when that bar has NaN open/high/low but a real close -- a shape `app.portfolio.pricing._latest_close` doesn't guard against (it only checks `close` for NaN when deriving `position.current_price`, at pricing.py line 104). When that happens, `daily_by_id[e.position.id]`'s last row becomes yesterday's bar, so `evaluate_exit_flags`'s `latest_close = daily_close.iloc[-1]` (app/portfolio/exits.py) silently reads yesterday's close instead of today's -- violating evaluate_exit_flags's own documented 'daily_ohlcv and position.current_price must be as-of the same trading day' precondition, which held before this PR (the router previously passed the same unfiltered frame `_latest_close` derived `current_price` from, so the two were guaranteed to agree by construction). Reproduced end-to-end via TestClient against the real /api/portfolio/risk endpoint: a position whose today's real close (90.0) is below its protective stop (98.33...) -- which docs/Analyse.md #7 says must raise 'stop_hit' regardless of Screen 2/3 state -- gets `exit_flags: []` on this PR's branch, while the identical fixture against origin/main (pre-PR) correctly returns `exit_flags: ['stop_hit']`. This is a genuine, demonstrated regression: a real stop-hit is now silently suppressed for this malformed-bar shape -- exactly the class of hazard (a real signal silently swallowed by a NaN-adjacent comparison) this whole PR/task line exists to prevent, just reached via a different path than the one it fixed. protective_stop's own lookback window also silently shifts back by one day in this scenario (a secondary symptom of the same root cause: the filtered frame is one row shorter than the caller assumes). Neither new regression test (test_malformed_bar_earlier_in_history_does_not_perturb_stop_or_flags, test_malformed_bar_that_drops_history_below_minimum_excludes_position) covers 'latest bar: real close, other OHLC fields NaN' -- both place the malformed bar earlier in history or fully NaN including close. This needs a fix before merge: e.g. deriving position.current_price from the same drop_malformed_daily_bars-filtered frame in app.portfolio.pricing (so current_price and daily_ohlcv's last row can never disagree), or excluding a position outright in get_risk when filtering changes which row is 'latest', rather than silently proceeding with the two out of sync.

Non-blocking: test_malformed_bar_earlier_in_history_does_not_perturb_stop_or_flags places its injected malformed row at the very oldest position in the frame, where pandas' ewm(adjust=False)/skipna aggregations happen to make dropping it a no-op regardless of whether drop_malformed_daily_bars is actually called -- verified by reverting the router fix locally, this test still passes. It therefore doesn't discriminate the fix the way test_malformed_bar_that_drops_history_below_minimum_excludes_position does. Tracked as a follow-up task rather than blocking, since the production fix itself is still correct and general (drop_malformed_daily_bars drops a NaN row unconditionally, regardless of position in the frame).

review.notes: Backend suite: 481 passed, 99.84% coverage (100% on both changed files), tsc/eslint clean, openapi.json/types.ts confirmed genuinely regenerate to a no-op diff (docstring-only). verify-elder-signal and code-review skills found no methodology/style issues in the diff itself; the blocking finding above was found via manual cross-file tracing (pricing.py's _latest_close only NaN-guards `close`, not open/high/low) plus an end-to-end TestClient reproduction against both this branch and origin/main to confirm it's a genuine, PR-introduced regression rather than a pre-existing gap. The weekly_ohlcv-filtering deferral (checklist item 2 / decisions entry 3) is a sound, well-reasoned call -- speculative absent an observed malformed weekly bar, and non-trivial to do correctly given evaluate_tide's index-alignment invariant across evaluate_exit_flags's two calls -- no finding there. Filed docs/tasks/api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators-followups-followups.json for the one non-blocking finding.
